newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Ausdoc sells office products unit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Ausdoc sells office products unit.

text.p: Ausdoc Group Ltd said on Thursday it has sold its office products supply business, Ausdoc Office, to an Australian subsidiary of Blue Star Group Ltd, a New Zealand based subsidiary of US Office Products Co.
Ausdoc said Ausdoc Office was sold on an ungeared basis for about A$43 million, comprising A$10 million for the tangible assets and A$33 million for the goodwill.

"The decision to sell our Ausdoc Office division was reached following extensive deliberation as to the future focus of the activities of Ausdoc Group," managing director Peter Reilly said in a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange.
"Our intention is to focus on our core information storage and document transfer businesses," he said.

Reilly said that over the past three years, Ausdoc had pursued a disciplined process of disposing of its printing businesses, reducing the scale of its retail activities and expanding its contract and commercial stationery interests both organically and by acquisition.
Reilly said the sale represented a book profit of A$14.5 million after capital gains tax of A$7 million. Ausdoc will receive the full purchase price in cash on December 30.
"We will initially apply the proceeds to pay down debt," Reilly said.
"However, we are actively considering how to maximise shareholder value," he said.

"We continue to review possible acquisitions in the document exchange, courier and records management markets but have not presently identified any significant opportunities which meet our investment requirements," he said.
"We will also consider a share buyback programme or a return of capital to shareholders," Reilly said.

He described Ausdoc Office was one of Australia's largest contract suppliers of office products. "However, it is not possible to ignore the trend of globalisation of the contract supply office products industry," he said.

"Some players have been aggressively pursuing growth through acquisition and the price offered by the purchaser meant we could maximise our return for shareholders from the realisation of the business, rather than through operating the business ourselves," Reilly said.
U.S Office Products recently bought 100 percent of Blue Star and subsequently the Whitcoulls Group in New Zealand to make the company the leading contract office supplier in that country.
Ausdoc shares were one cent lower at A$1.45 at 10.45 a.m. (0045 GMT) on Thursday.
